brief.subject: No new EUDR moves today; coffee and cocoa supply in focus
brief.headline: Quiet day for EUDR news as coffee logistics and food-crop costs make headlines
brief.dek: No new EUDR guidance or enforcement surfaced today; Starbucks touts inventory gains and rice joins cocoa as a cost worry.
brief.lede: Today's sources contain no new EUDR deadlines, guidance or enforcement actions. Two supply-chain stories touch coffee and cocoa, two commodities the regulation covers.

sections.heading: Starbucks says shelves are fuller
bullets: Starbucks' CEO says inventory availability is at an all-time high, helped by daily deliveries.
The chain is trialing a 24-hour operating model to make its supply chain faster and more dependable.
The report does not mention EUDR or deforestation checks on coffee sourcing.

sections.heading: After cocoa, rice costs bite
bullets: Climate disruption and higher rice prices are pushing food makers to rework recipes and sourcing.
Cited examples include Kellogg's Rice Krispies and Japanese rice crackers.
The story frames rice as following cocoa into supply trouble; rice itself is not an EUDR commodity.

brief.seo_description: EUDR brief: no new rules or enforcement today. Starbucks reports record inventory availability; rising rice costs follow cocoa's squeeze.

items.title: Starbucks inventory availability at ‘all-time high’ with daily deliveries, CEO says
items.snippet: The coffeehouse chain has been testing a 24-hour operating model to improve inventory availability and build an overall faster, more reliable supply chain.

items.title: First cocoa, now rice: Is another food crisis brewing?
items.snippet: From Kellogg's Rice Krispies to Japan's rice crackers, climate disruption and rising rice costs are forcing food manufacturers to rethink recipes and sourcing.
